o: The murmur gets louder as pulmonary hypertension develops
It increases the risk of brain abscess
The smallest defects produce the softest murmurs
There is no risk of endocarditis
The characteristic murmur is pansystolic at the left sternal border
e: Small defects give loud murmurs; pulmonary hypertension makes the murmur softer.

q: Right ventricular hypertrophy is seen in all EXCEPT:
e: A patent ductus arteriosus causes left ventricular hypertrophy (volume load of the left heart).

q: Regarding left-to-right shunts, which is NOT true?
o: A ventricular septal defect causes biventricular hypertrophy
The ECG in patent ductus arteriosus shows right ventricular hypertrophy
An atrial septal defect causes right ventricular hypertrophy
e: A patent ductus arteriosus shows left ventricular hypertrophy; right ventricular hypertrophy appears only with pulmonary hypertension.

q: Which congenital lesion is least likely to cause infective endocarditis?
e: The pressure difference across an atrial septal defect is low.

q: A loud pulmonary second sound in a child with a large ventricular septal defect indicates:
e: A loud P2 means pulmonary hypertension.

q: A parasternal heave is NOT expected in:
e: A parasternal heave means right ventricular hypertrophy; a patent ductus arteriosus loads the left ventricle.

q: A 6-week-old is breathless during feeds and has a loud pansystolic murmur at the lower left sternal edge and a liver 3 cm below the costal margin. What is the best confirmatory test?
e: Echocardiography is diagnostic for a ventricular septal defect.

q: A 9-year-old has headache and a blood pressure of 150/95 mmHg in the arm; the femoral pulses are weak and delayed. What is the diagnosis?
e: Radio-femoral delay with hypertension in the arm indicates coarctation of the aorta.

q: What is the key auscultatory sign of an atrial septal defect?
o: Wide fixed splitting of the second heart sound
e: Constant overfilling of the right ventricle fixes the split.

q: A preterm infant on day 5 has a systolic murmur below the left clavicle and bounding pulses and is hard to wean from the ventilator. What is the treatment?
e: A patent ductus arteriosus in a preterm baby is closed medically.

q: A newborn on day 5 is in shock with absent femoral pulses. The first drug is:
e: The systemic circulation depends on the duct (coarctation), so prostaglandin E1 is given.
